To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) school climate perceptions were significantly related to student intrinsic motivation; (2) student intrinsic motivation was significantly related to teacher ratings of student engagement; (3) teacher ratings of student intrinsic motivation were significantly related to academic performance; and (4) student perceptions of school climate were significantly related to teacher-rated student academic engagement, and (5) student perceptions of the school climate were indirectly related to academic performance via student intrinsic motivation and student academic engagement.

school climate factors, such as fairness, safety, and enjoyment, are important predictors of student intrinsic motivation, and that teacher ratings of student engagement mediate the relationship between school climate and academic performance.

(1) the school environment has a significant influence on students’ academic performance, (2) this influence is mediated by students’ perceptions of their school climate, (3) students’ perceptions of the school environment influence their academic engagement, and (4) teachers’ ratings of academic engagement are influenced by students’ perceptions.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a model that can be used to guide school reform efforts to enhance student motivation, academic achievement, and academic engagement among urban, African American middle school youth.
understanding the processes through which school climate factors relate to academic outcomes among African American middle school children placed at risk.
how school climate factors relate to student academic achievement and how these factors may affect students differently.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
school climate is a very important factor in the academic performance of urban students placed at-risk.
the school environment is important for urban African American children and their academic achievement, and that teachers can have an impact on this environment.
the school environment has a direct effect on academic performance through the mediation of intrinsic motivation and teacher-rated academic engagement.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a school climate that is fair and enjoyable is associated with higher student motivation and academic engagement, which in turn are associated with better academic achievement among urban African American students.
the school environment, particularly the social climate, has a significant influence on student motivation, academic engagement, and achievement.
the students' perception of the school climate was a strong predictor of their intrinsic motivation and academic engagement.
The main takeaway from our work is that

schools should be places where students feel safe, where students and teachers have a positive and respectful relationship, where students feel they are treated fairly, and where students are actively involved in their learning.
school climate factors are important for understanding academic achievement in urban African American students.
